fullPassage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like 'his face just popped out at me,' that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.

(A) David Dunning found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features can actually be a <u>sign</u> of an inaccurate identification. In other words, thinking too hard about a face may mean you got it wrong.
(B) Please <u>sign</u> your name at the bottom of the contract before you hand it back to the office manager.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 sign이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 표지판 — (B) 서명하다: (A)는 도로 표지판이 아니라 '~라는 징후'라는 뜻
❌ ② (A) 징후 — (B) 신호를 보내다: (B)는 계약서에 이름을 적는 '서명하다'이지 신호를 보내는 것이 아님
✅ ③ (A) 징후 — (B) 서명하다: (A)는 부정확한 식별의 '징후/조짐'(명사), (B)는 이름을 적는 '서명하다'(동사) ←정답
❌ ④ (A) 서명 — (B) 징후: 두 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
det.tip: sign: (명사) 징후, 조짐 vs (동사) 서명하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a choice that you make about what to do after thinking about several possibilities"

det.korean: decision=결정: 여러 가능성을 생각한 후 무엇을 할지 정하는 선택
det.analysis:
❌ ① reaction: reaction(반응)은 자극에 대한 즉각적 대응이지 심사숙고 후의 선택이 아님
❌ ② procedure: procedure(절차)는 일을 하는 정해진 방법
❌ ③ impression: impression(인상)은 느낌·인상이지 '무엇을 할지 정하는 선택'이 아님
✅ ④ decision: decision(결정)은 여러 가능성을 고려한 후 하는 선택이라는 영영 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
det.tip: decision = 결정 (여러 선택지를 고려한 뒤 내리는 선택)

questions.passage: David Dunning found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed __________ (discuss) of selection procedures can be a sign of an inaccurate identification.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 동사 discuss를 명사 discussion으로 변환. 'a detailed _____ of selection procedures'에서 앞에 관사 a와 형용사 detailed가 있고 뒤에 of가 이어지므로, 이 자리에는 명사가 와야 함. 따라서 discussion(논의)이 알맞음.
det.tip: discuss(논의하다) → discussion(논의). 'a detailed _____' 뒤 명사 자리

questions.passage: Malcolm Gladwell describes studies that demonstrate the superior __________ (perform) of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 동사 perform을 명사 performance로 변환. 'the superior _____ of relatively unconscious first guesses'에서 앞에 the와 형용사 superior가 있고 뒤에 of가 이어지므로 명사 자리임. 따라서 performance(성과)가 알맞음.
det.tip: perform(수행하다) → performance(성과). 'the superior _____ of' 명사 자리

questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like 'his face just popped out at me,' that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very __________ can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: first impression=첫인상. 바로 그 '첫인상'이 세상에 대해 더 정확할 수 있음
det.analysis:
✅ ① first impression: 원문 일치. 'That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world'에서 바로 그 '첫인상' ←정답
❌ ② final decision: final decision(최종 결정)은 심사숙고의 결과로 글의 방향과 반대
❌ ③ careful analysis: careful analysis(신중한 분석)는 글이 오히려 부정확하다고 보는 대상
❌ ④ logical reasoning: logical reasoning(논리적 추론)도 첫인상과 대비되는 것으로 빈칸에 부적절
det.tip: That very first impression = 바로 그 첫인상 (글의 핵심 소재)

questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like 'his face just popped out at me,' that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively __________ compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: unconscious first guesses=무의식적인 첫 추측. 이것이 논리적 정당화보다 우수함
det.analysis:
❌ ① logical step-by-step plans: 뒤에 'compared to logical step-by-step justifications'와 대비되는 대상이 빈칸이므로, 논리적 계획은 대비의 반대편이라 부적절
✅ ② unconscious first guesses: 원문 일치. 'the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses'에서 무의식적 '첫 추측' ←정답
❌ ③ careful written reports: careful written reports(신중한 서면 보고)는 무의식적 판단과 반대
❌ ④ detailed group discussions: detailed group discussions(상세한 그룹 토론)도 즉각적·무의식적 판단과 상반
det.tip: unconscious first guesses = 무의식적인 첫 추측 (논리적 정당화보다 우수)
